title: Content Specialist - Video, Static Images, etc (Meta) | NZ Agency
description:
Graphic Designer & Video Editor (part-time, long-term)



We're a small marketing agency in New Zealand. We do marketing for financial advisers, mostly mortgage and insurance advisers and KiwiSaver specialists. We're looking for someone to take creative production off our plate (with our overseeing) so we can focus on growing the business.



What you'd actually be doing



Your main job is static design. Meta ad images, carousels, social graphics, landing page visuals and the odd
 header, across a handful of client brands.



The second part is video. Clients and our team film short-form content, usually talking-head style on a phone, and you turn it into ads and Reels people actually watch. Cutting, pacing, captions, hooks in the first few seconds, and exporting the right versions for each placement.



We write the brief and set the direction, and we sign off anything a client or consumer will see. Past that, the craft is yours. You d
 the layout, the crop, the cut and what makes the scroll stop.



A bonus if you can do it: publishing blog posts to WordPress and scheduling social posts. Not required, but that would be highly valued.



Please read this bit before applying:

Static design is the core of this role, and it's where we need you strongest.



We see a lot of applications from video editors who can put a graphic together in Canva when they need to. There's nothing wrong with that, but it isn't this job. If your design experience is "I've made some posts", please save us both the time. We do test this properly, and there's no clever way to talk your way around a portfolio.



What we need



3+ years designing for paid social or digital marketing. Agency-side ideally, since you'd be moving between client brands here



A strong static portfolio. Ads that were built to perform, not just look nice



Solid short-form video editing. Reels, TikTok and Meta video ads in 9:16, 4:5 and 1:1, with clean captions and good pacing



Confident in Figma, or Canva for design, and Premiere Pro, or CapCut for video



You can work inside someone else's brand guidelines without it looking like a template



Good written English. You'll be taking briefs in writing and you'll be in our Slack every day



Online 7am to 11am Manila time. We're based in New Zealand and need to be able to communicate during business hours.



Nice to have but not required: financial services, mortgage or insurance marketing. Motion graphics or After Effects. WordPress. Social scheduling tools like Metricool or GoHighLevel. Basic copywriting.



What we're like to work for

Our clients are licensed financial advisers, which means there are real legal rules about what their ads can say. So any text a consumer will read, headlines, on-screen captions, anything mentioning rates, comes from us or gets checked by us first. Don't add or change wording on a creative without running it past us.



Every file gets saved to the right client folder, named properly, with editable source files kept. That's the one thing we're strict about. It's how we stay out of your way without losing track of what's been made.



If you're going to miss a deadline, tell us the same day. Nobody here gets in trouble for bad news arriving early.



You'll always know what you're working towards, because every piece of work comes with a written brief.



This is part-time and long-term, a direct contract with us. No agency in the middle taking a cut. Paid every fortnight through Wise on the 15th and the 30th. We've never paid anyone late and we don't intend to start with you.



How to apply

Please don't send a template. We read every application and we can spot one from the first line.



Your portfolio, with at least 5 static ads or social graphics and 2 short-form videos you edited. Tell us which ones you're proudest of and why



Tell us about a creative that performed well or badly. What was the idea, what did you do, and what did you learn from how it went. Under 250 words, real numbers if you have them



Tell us straight whether you're stronger at design or at video, and why



Your CV or profile, any blog or social posting experience, and the hourly rate you're looking for in USD

Start your message with the word ORCHARD so we know you got this far



If you're shortlisted we'll send you a real brief: one static ad and one short video edit from raw footage. It takes about 90 minutes and we pay you your rate for it, because your time is worth something before you work here as well as after.



Then a video call. We're hoping to have someone chosen by Oct 10th.



Looking forward to hearing from you!

description:
We are looking for a reliable, creative YouTube video editor to join the J.Crew Coaching content team on an ongoing basis.



The channel follows an IFBB Pro bodybuilder, coach, husband, and father documenting his “Road Back” to the competitive stage. The content blends bodybuilding, coaching education, family life, mindset, and behind-the-scenes storytelling.



WHAT YOU’LL EDIT

• Occasional vertical clips/Shorts repurposed from the main episode

• Raw footage may include training, talking-head commentary, family/lifestyle moments, client coaching, and competition prep



WHAT WE NEED

• Strong storytelling instincts—not just flashy effects

• Clean, modern edits with strong pacing and viewer retention

• Ability to organize raw footage and build a clear story

• Understanding of hooks, retention, pattern interrupts, and emotional story beats

• Bonus: experience creating YouTube Shorts or thumbnails



WORKFLOW

• First cut expected within 3–5 days of receiving footage

• Feedback will be clear and organized

• We are looking for a long-term working relationship with room to grow

2. Send 2–3 links to your best long-form YouTube edits.

3. Briefly explain your editing process and typical turnaround time.

title: Klaviyo Email Marketing Manager (E-commerce)
description:
About Us



We are an e-commerce company operating multiple brands across different markets, including the USA and France. We are a fast-growing team focused on building and scaling high-quality e-commerce brands through strong creative content and performance marketing.



We run everything in house: paid advertising, our Shopify stores, customer service, logistics and
. We launch new stores and enter new markets regularly, so the role you start with is not the role you will have in a year.



We're looking for a Klaviyo
 Marketing Manager to take full ownership of
 across our stores.



The Role



 is one of our biggest revenue channels, and we want you to be responsible for running Klaviyo across all our brands: campaigns, flows, segments and reporting.



We are not looking for a Klaviyo genius. We are looking for someone reliable, someone who checks their work before it goes out and notices when something is broken without being asked. The technical side can be taught. The person currently handling this role will train you on every brand.



Your Responsibilities



- Plan and build weekly promotional campaigns across our stores

- Write and adapt campaign copy for each market, using AI tools and editing the output so it sounds right for that country

- Create or edit campaign visuals ( AI, Canva... ) 

- Manage lists and segments, including language segmentation on bilingual stores

- Check the accounts daily for anything broken: bounces, spam complaints, dead links, expired codes

- Audit and improve the automated flows (welcome, abandoned checkout, post-purchase, winback)

- Run A/B tests on subject lines, offers, flows, send times and creatives

- Send a weekly performance report

- Keep competitor research updated on a list we provide, plus brands you find yourself

- Keep everything documented and up to date in ClickUp



What We're Looking For



- Working Klaviyo experience is a must: lists, segments, campaign building, scheduling...

- Strong attention to detail. This matters more than anything else in this role. Several accounts across several countries means a lot of small things that must be right: the correct segment, a working link, the right currency, no typo.

- Practical use of AI tools for copy and visuals, with the judgement to edit the output rather than ship it raw

- Ability to adapt to different countries, products and brand voices

- Ability to work independently and follow a checklist without being chased

- Reliable communication and respected deadlines

- English good enough to communicate clearly in writing. It does not need to be perfect.

- Shopify basics: discount codes, product pages, UTM tracking



Tools



Experience with some of the following is a plus:



- ClickUp

- Google Drive

- Shopify

- Canva / Figma

- ChatGPT / Claude

- AI image generation tools



You don't need to know every tool listed above. What matters most is your reliability and your ability to learn new tools quickly.



How We Hire



We will select 3 candidates. All 3 get the same missions on different stores. We work with all 3 for 2 weeks, then we keep the one who was the most implicate. We tell you this openly so you know exactly where you stand, and the 2 weeks are paid whatever happens.



Trial: part time, $4 USD per hour, for 2 weeks



Then: if we keep working together, a full time position at $600/month for your first 2 months while we train you on all the brands



After that: once you are more autonomous, we discuss a raise. The more of the channel you can run without us, the more we can pay you.



We start by telling you what to do, and within a few months we want you proposing the campaigns instead of receiving them.



What We Offer



- Remote position

- Fully flexible schedule. We don't mind when you work. What we measure is the work: campaigns out on time, nothing broken, reports delivered.

- Work across multiple e-commerce brands and markets

- Proper brief from the person currently in the role

- Full ownership of the channel, no layers of approval

- Room to grow within a fast-growing e-commerce company

- Long-term collaboration for the right person



How to Apply



Tell us a bit about yourself, in your own words. No cover letter needed.



Who you are and what you've worked on. What kind of brands or clients, and what you actually did for them.

How comfortable you are with Klaviyo, ClickUp and Google Drive. Be honest: "I use it daily", "I've used it a few times" and "I've never touched it" are all fine answers.



When you could start.



Do you have anything else on the side right now, a job, freelance clients or studies? This will not disqualify you, we just want the real picture.



If you do have something else and you want to keep it: why, and how do you see yourself handling both?

title: Finance Officer
description:
About Us:



Astute Early Years Specialists is an Australian early childhood education consultancy based in Brisbane, supporting

childcare providers and a portfolio of early learning centres across Australia. We’re hiring a full-time, remote

Finance Officer to help run day-to-day finance across our centres — accounts payable and receivable,

reconciliations, month-end journals, on-charging, and reporting support — using Xero and our wider finance

stack.



This is a direct-hire contractor role (not through an agency). You’ll work closely with our CFO and Finance team in

Brisbane. We’re after a qualified accountant who wants to own their work and get it right, every time.



We are based in Australia (AEST), so your timezone lines up well with ours — that is a genuine plus for us.



Scope of Role:



• Manage end-to-end accounts payable and receivable in Xero — invoice checking, entry, approvals, payment

runs, and debtor follow-up



• Reconcile transactions via Hubdoc and Budgetly with correct coding and on-charging



• Complete weekly on-charge reconciliations across multiple centres and related entities



• Create and post end-of-month journals; assist with BAS and balance sheet reconciliations



• Support fortnightly payroll processing for allocated centres (PAYG, superannuation, leave)



• Help prepare monthly management accounts, variance analysis, and cashflow forecasts



• Contribute to dashboards and KPI tracking (e.g. Occupancy, WRA%)



• Keep records audit-ready and suggest ways to streamline finance processes





Skills & Experience:



• You must be a qualified accountant — a bachelor’s degree in accountancy (or equivalent, Philippines) held or

in progress. This is essential, not a “nice to have”

• 3+ years running accounts payable/receivable, reconciliations and month-end in a finance role

• Hands-on Xero experience

• Strong grasp of core accounting principles and month-end processes

• Strong Excel / Google Sheets skills

• High attention to detail and comfortable owning deadlines

• Excellent written and spoken English

• Ability to work a shift with real-time overlap into Australian business hours (AEST/AEDT)

• Reliable high-speed internet and a proper home-office setup





Nice to Have:



• Exposure to Hubdoc, Budgetly, Fathom or Employment Hero

• Experience in a multi-entity accounting environment

• Exposure to Australian accounting standards and compliance (BAS, GST, PAYG, super)

• Experience working remotely for an Australian employer

• Exposure to the Australian childcare / ECEC sector



The Opportunity:



- Remote, offshore role with a structured and supportive finance team.

- Own a portfolio of childcare centres with real accountability.

- Work where your accuracy directly drives business decisions.

- We value ownership—you treat deadlines as fixed and proactively resolve issues.





HOW TO APPLY:



To show you've read the entire job advertisement, start your application with the word "INTERESTED"



Please also include:



A brief summary of your accounting and payroll experience (Australian payroll experience is essential)

A Google Drive link containing your updated resume / cover letter

Your expected monthly salary

Your notice period and earliest available start date



We look forward to hearing from you!

title: BILLING REVENUE CYCLE MANAGER
description:
BILLING REVENUE CYCLE MANAGER



Reports To



Operations Director, Finance Director, and/or Executive Director



Position Type



Full-Time



Organization



Wings of the Future, NFP



Position Summary



Wings of the Future, NFP is seeking an experienced, dependable, and detail-oriented Billing Revenue Cycle Manager to oversee the organization’s complete revenue cycle.



This is a full-time leadership position responsible for ensuring that services are accurately documented, claims are submitted correctly and on time, payments are properly posted, denied and unpaid claims are actively resolved, and accounts receivable remains current and manageable.



The Billing Revenue Cycle Manager will supervise daily billing operations and coordinate with leadership, providers, clinical staff, intake personnel, administrative team members, and insurance payers. The manager will establish effective billing workflows, monitor staff performance, identify revenue-cycle problems, reduce preventable denials, and provide leadership with accurate financial and operational reports.



A central responsibility of this position is ensuring the correct setup and maintenance of clients’ primary and secondary insurance coverage. The successful candidate must understand coordination of benefits, payer order, claim sequencing, crossover claims, secondary billing, authorizations, remittance processing, denial management, payment posting, reconciliation, and accounts-receivable follow-up.



This position does not include provider credentialing or payer-enrollment duties.



Role Purpose



To lead the organization’s billing and revenue-cycle operations from eligibility verification through final payment resolution while protecting compliance, reducing revenue leakage, supporting organizational growth, and maintaining accurate, audit-ready billing records.



Essential Duties and Responsibilities



1. Revenue Cycle Leadership and Oversight



* Manage the complete revenue cycle from client intake and insurance verification through claim submission, payment posting, denial resolution, reconciliation, and final account disposition.

* Establish, document, and maintain billing policies, procedures, workflows, timelines, and accountability standards.

* Monitor daily, weekly, and monthly billing activity to ensure claims and follow-up tasks are completed accurately and on time.

* Identify workflow breakdowns, revenue leakage, billing delays, and recurring claim problems.

* Develop corrective-action plans and monitor progress until identified issues are resolved.

* Coordinate billing activities across clinical, intake, administrative, and financial departments.

* Ensure billing staff understand their assignments, deadlines, escalation responsibilities, and performance expectations.

* Provide leadership with clear information about billing performance, outstanding revenue, operational risks, and recommended solutions.



2. Primary and Secondary Insurance Setup and Coordination



* Oversee the accurate setup and maintenance of primary and secondary insurance profiles in the billing system and electronic health record.

* Ensure payer names, member and group numbers, plan types, effective and termination dates, subscriber information, relationships to subscribers, claims addresses, payer IDs, and other required information are entered correctly.

* Confirm which insurance coverage is primary and which is secondary using payer information and applicable coordination-of-benefits requirements.

* Ensure staff do not guess when payer order, eligibility, benefits, or coordination of benefits is unclear.

* Confirm active coverage, benefits, patient responsibility, authorization requirements, and payer-specific billing rules before claims are submitted.

* Resolve or escalate coverage conflicts, inactive policies, duplicate coverage, missing information, and coordination-of-benefits problems.

* Oversee the correct sequencing of primary and secondary claims.

* Ensure required primary-payer remittance information is submitted to secondary payers.

* Track crossover claims and ensure secondary claims are manually submitted when automatic crossover does not occur.

* Prevent duplicate billing, incorrect payer billing, untimely filing, and avoidable denials related to insurance setup or payer order.



3. Claim Preparation, Review, and Submission



* Oversee the preparation, review, batching, submission, and tracking of claims.

* Review claims for accuracy before submission when additional oversight is required.

* Confirm the accuracy of client demographics, insurance information, payer information, rendering and billing provider data, dates of service, CPT and HCPCS codes, ICD-10 codes, modifiers, units, place of service, authorizations, and other required claim elements.

* Ensure missing, incomplete, inconsistent, or incorrect information is corrected before claim submission.

* Monitor compliance with payer-specific billing requirements and timely-filing deadlines.

* Ensure clean claims are submitted promptly after billing documentation is completed.

* Maintain accurate claim-submission records, billing logs, and supporting documentation.

* Establish quality-control procedures to reduce rejected claims, denied claims, and delayed reimbursement.



4. Documentation and Billing Readiness



* Establish and oversee procedures for determining whether services are ready to be billed.

* Confirm that required service notes, signatures, dates, treatment plans, assessments, authorizations, service logs, and supporting records are present.

* Monitor outstanding documentation and ensure providers and supervisors receive timely notification when records are missing or incomplete.

* Track documentation delays that prevent billing and report unresolved concerns to the appropriate clinical or organizational leader.

* Identify documentation patterns that contribute to claim delays, denials, recoupments, or audit risk.

* Coordinate with clinical leadership regarding documentation concerns without replacing clinical supervision or making unauthorized clinical decisions.

* Ensure claims are not knowingly submitted without the required supporting documentation.



5. Eligibility, Benefits, and Authorization Management



* Oversee eligibility and benefit verification at intake and throughout the course of service delivery.

* Confirm coverage dates, benefit limitations, deductibles, copayments, coinsurance, authorization requirements, and payer-specific restrictions.

* Maintain accurate records of authorization numbers, approved dates, authorized units, service types, expiration dates, and payer requirements.

* Monitor authorization usage and ensure leadership and clinical staff are notified when an authorization is missing, incorrect, exhausted, denied, or approaching expiration.

* Prevent services from being billed under expired, invalid, or incorrect authorizations.

* Review payer portals and communicate coverage or authorization concerns promptly.

* Develop processes for rechecking eligibility at appropriate intervals.



6. Payment Posting and Reconciliation



* Oversee the accurate posting of insurance payments, patient payments, contractual adjustments, denials, refunds, recoupments, and patient responsibility.

* Review EOBs, ERAs, electronic-funds-transfer reports, payment reports, and payer portals.

* Ensure payments and adjustments are correctly matched to claims and client accounts.

* Reconcile payments received against bank deposits, electronic remittances, payer reports, and billing-system records.

* Identify and investigate unapplied payments, underpayments, overpayments, incorrect adjustments, missing payments, recoupments, and other discrepancies.

* Monitor credit balances and coordinate appropriate corrections, refunds, or account adjustments.

* Complete or oversee monthly billing reconciliation.

* Maintain organized financial records that support internal review, financial reporting, and audits.



7. Accounts Receivable Management



* Manage insurance and patient accounts receivable.

* Review aging reports routinely and assign follow-up priorities based on claim age, balance, payer, filing deadline, and likelihood of collection.

* Establish follow-up standards for unpaid, pending, denied, rejected, underpaid, and partially paid claims.

* Monitor balances in the 0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 91–120, and over-120-day aging categories.

* Develop action plans to reduce older accounts receivable and prevent new billing backlogs.

* Ensure billing staff document all payer contacts, reference numbers, claim statuses, corrections, and next-action dates.

* Escalate high-dollar, high-risk, or long-outstanding claims to leadership when necessary.

* Recommend accounts for appeal, reconsideration, adjustment, payment plan, collection activity, or write-off according to organizational policy.

* Do not authorize write-offs, refunds, or material adjustments without the required leadership approval.



8. Denial, Rejection, and Claim Follow-Up



* Oversee the tracking and resolution of denied, rejected, unpaid, pending, delayed, and underpaid claims.

* Research denial and rejection reasons and ensure the appropriate corrective action is taken.

* Prepare or supervise corrected claims, reconsiderations, appeals, medical-necessity submissions, and payer follow-up.

* Ensure claims are corrected and resubmitted within payer deadlines.

* Gather and submit supporting documentation when authorized and required.

* Monitor appeal deadlines and maintain complete appeal records.

* Identify recurring denial patterns by payer, provider, service, diagnosis, procedure code, modifier, authorization, location, or documentation issue.

* Conduct root-cause analysis and recommend workflow, training, documentation, or system corrections.

* Maintain denial reports that show volume, dollar amount, cause, responsible department, action taken, and final outcome.

* Track overturned denials and recovered revenue.



9. Patient Balances and Financial Communication



* Ensure patient responsibility is calculated, posted, and communicated accurately.

* Oversee the preparation and review of patient statements.

* Support the resolution of client billing questions in a professional, respectful, and confidential manner.

* Ensure staff explain balances without making unauthorized guarantees about payer coverage or payment.

* Coordinate approved payment arrangements according to organizational policy.

* Address disputed balances by reviewing payments, adjustments, claim activity, benefits, and supporting records.

* Escalate sensitive or unresolved billing disputes to leadership.



10. Billing Team Supervision



* Supervise billing specialists, billing assistants, contractors, and other assigned revenue-cycle personnel.

* Assign work and establish daily, weekly, and monthly priorities.

* Train staff on billing procedures, payer requirements, documentation standards, system use, confidentiality, and escalation expectations.

* Review staff work for accuracy, timeliness, completeness, and compliance.

* Conduct regular billing meetings, individual check-ins, and performance reviews.

* Provide coaching and corrective feedback when performance standards are not met.

* Track staff productivity, claim volume, follow-up activity, error rates, and completion of assigned tasks.

* Ensure appropriate billing coverage during staff absences.

* Promote accountability while maintaining a professional and respectful working environment.

* Notify leadership promptly about serious errors, repeated noncompliance, suspected misconduct, or performance concerns.



11. Reporting and Performance Analysis



* Prepare weekly and monthly revenue-cycle reports for leadership.

* Track and report:

    * Charges entered

    * Claims submitted

    * Payments received

    * Adjustments

    * Denials and rejections

    * Outstanding accounts receivable

    * Aging by payer and provider

    * Days in accounts receivable

    * Clean-claim rate

    * First-pass acceptance rate

    * Denial rate

    * Collection rate

    * Net collection rate

    * Underpayments

    * Authorization-related delays

    * Unbilled services

    * Documentation-related billing holds

    * Secondary claims awaiting submission or payment

    * High-dollar outstanding claims

    * Recovered revenue

* Explain significant changes, trends, risks, and unresolved concerns.

* Provide realistic recommendations for improving collections, reducing delays, and strengthening internal controls.

* Maintain accurate reporting data and correct identified discrepancies promptly.



12. Payer Communication and Issue Resolution



* Communicate professionally with payer representatives, provider-service departments, claims departments, utilization-management teams, and other authorized contacts.

* Verify claim status and obtain clear explanations for delayed, denied, reduced, or recouped payments.

* Document payer calls, portal activity, reference numbers, representatives contacted, information received, and required next steps.

* Escalate unresolved payer problems through appropriate channels.

* Monitor payer bulletins, billing updates, claim requirements, and policy changes that affect reimbursement.

* Communicate relevant payer updates to leadership and affected staff.

* Maintain organized payer-specific billing guidance for internal use.



13. Compliance, Privacy, and Audit Readiness



* Maintain compliance with HIPAA, applicable billing regulations, payer requirements, contractual obligations, and organizational policies.

* Protect client, clinical, insurance, and financial information at all times.

* Maintain accurate, secure, complete, and audit-ready billing records.

* Ensure billing system access is limited to authorized personnel.

* Prohibit unauthorized changes to client accounts, claims, payments, adjustments, or financial records.

* Report suspected billing errors, overpayments, duplicate payments, privacy concerns, falsification, fraud, waste, abuse, or compliance problems promptly.

* Cooperate with internal reviews, payer audits, financial audits, and authorized compliance investigations.

* Help develop corrective-action plans when an audit or internal review identifies deficiencies.

* Never direct staff to submit unsupported, inaccurate, duplicate, or intentionally misleading claims.



14. Systems and Process Improvement



* Evaluate billing workflows and recommend practical improvements.

* Create and maintain standard operating procedures, checklists, dashboards, and tracking tools.

* Assist with billing-system setup, payer configuration, clearinghouse workflows, electronic remittance enrollment, and reporting functions as authorized.

* Identify automation opportunities that improve accuracy without weakening oversight or internal controls.

* Test billing-process changes before full implementation.

* Train affected staff when processes or payer requirements change.

* Support organizational expansion by developing billing workflows that can accommodate additional services, providers, programs, locations, and states.



Required Qualifications



* At least three years of progressively responsible healthcare billing or revenue-cycle experience.

* Demonstrated experience managing the complete claim cycle from eligibility verification through final payment resolution.

* Demonstrated ability to build and maintain primary and secondary insurance coverage in a billing system or electronic health record.

* Strong working knowledge of coordination of benefits, payer order, primary-to-secondary claim sequencing, crossover claims, EOB and ERA review, and secondary claim submission.

* Experience with claim submission, payment posting, accounts receivable, denial management, corrected claims, appeals, and reconciliation.

* Working knowledge of CPT and HCPCS codes, ICD-10 codes, modifiers, service units, place-of-service codes, authorizations, and timely-filing requirements.

* Experience using billing software, electronic health records, clearinghouses, spreadsheets,
, and payer portals.

* Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, communication, and deadline-management skills.

* Ability to protect confidential information and consistently follow HIPAA and organizational privacy requirements.

* Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, supervise staff, and escalate concerns appropriately.

* Ability to follow detailed procedures while also identifying opportunities for operational improvement.

* Willingness to ask for clarification rather than guess when billing rules or account information are unclear.



Preferred Qualifications



* Five or more years of healthcare revenue-cycle experience.

* At least two years of billing leadership, team supervision, or revenue-cycle management experience.

* Experience in behavioral health, mental health, substance-use treatment, nonprofit healthcare, or multisite healthcare billing.

* Experience billing Medicaid, Medicare, managed-care plans, commercial insurance, employee-assistance programs, and private-pay accounts.

* Experience managing billing across multiple programs, locations, provider types, or states.

* Experience with behavioral-health authorizations, utilization requirements, treatment documentation, and payer audits.

* Experience developing billing policies, dashboards, performance reports, and staff training materials.

* Experience reducing accounts receivable, denial rates, billing backlogs, and preventable revenue loss.



Core Competencies



* Revenue-cycle leadership

* Billing accuracy

* Financial accountability

* Claims analysis

* Denial prevention and resolution

* Accounts-receivable management

* Staff supervision and development

* Process improvement

* Critical thinking and problem-solving

* Clear professional communication

* Confidentiality and ethical judgment

* Organization and deadline management

* Calm decision-making under pressure

* Accountability and follow-through

* Mission alignment



Typical Daily and Weekly Activities



* Review billing dashboards, outstanding claims, aging reports, denials, rejections, and unbilled services.

* Confirm that primary and secondary insurance profiles are accurate.

* Monitor eligibility, benefits, authorizations, payer order, and claim-submission status.

* Review claims and supporting documentation for billing readiness.

* Assign claim follow-up and accounts-receivable priorities to billing staff.

* Monitor primary claims, secondary claims, crossover claims, corrected claims, appeals, and unpaid balances.

* Review EOBs, ERAs, payment postings, adjustments, and reconciliation records.

* Contact payers or supervise payer follow-up on unresolved claims.

* Meet with billing staff to review assignments, challenges, deadlines, and performance.

* Communicate documentation or authorization concerns to the appropriate clinical or administrative staff.

* Provide leadership with billing updates, financial trends, risks, and recommended actions.

* Update procedures, trackers, reports, and internal billing resources as needed.



Performance Expectations and Success Measures



Success in this position will be measured by:



* Accurate and timely claim submission

* Accurate maintenance of primary and secondary insurance records

* Correct payer sequencing

* Improved clean-claim and first-pass acceptance rates

* Reduced claim rejections and preventable denials

* Timely denial correction and appeal submission

* Reduced accounts-receivable aging

* Fewer claims over 90 and 120 days

* Improved collection rates and revenue recovery

* Accurate payment posting and monthly reconciliation

* Timely identification of underpayments, overpayments, and recoupments

* Reduced billing backlog and unbilled-service volume

* Consistent authorization tracking

* Accurate and timely leadership reports

* Organized, current, secure, and audit-ready billing records

* Effective supervision and accountability of billing staff

* Clear communication and dependable follow-through

* Protection of confidential client and financial information

* Continued improvement in revenue-cycle performance



Training and Supervision



Leadership will provide orientation regarding the organization’s programs, systems, workflows, documentation standards, payer procedures, reporting expectations, confidentiality requirements, and compliance policies.



The Billing Revenue Cycle Manager is expected to take ownership of the department, maintain organized procedures, ask appropriate questions, incorporate feedback, train assigned billing staff, and demonstrate increasing independence and leadership.



This position requires consistent communication with the Operations Director, Finance Director, Executive Director, and other designated organizational leaders.



Confidentiality



This position has access to sensitive client, clinical, insurance, and financial information. Strict confidentiality and compliance with all applicable privacy laws, ethical standards, payer requirements, and organizational policies are conditions of employment.



Unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or removal of confidential information is prohibited. A breach of confidentiality, intentional falsification of billing information, unauthorized claim submission, concealment of billing errors, or misuse of financial records may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination.



Mission Alignment



Accurate and ethical revenue-cycle management allows Wings of the Future, NFP to remain financially stable, support its providers, serve its clients, and expand services for individuals and families in need.

title: Website Developer & Manager — Shopify Liquid and WordPress
description:
Full-time remote position | Philippines-based applicants welcome



Journey Psyche and Lyons Cards are seeking an experienced website developer to manage and improve our existing WordPress and Shopify websites.



Journey Psyche provides mental health services. Lyons Cards sells sports cards and collectibles and produces live card shows and breaks. You must be comfortable supporting both businesses.



We need someone who takes ownership of website performance, completes work reliably and flags problems promptly.



Responsibilities



* Maintain and improve Journey Psyche’s WordPress website and Lyons Cards’ Shopify store.

* Customize Shopify themes using Liquid, HTML, CSS and JavaScript—not just page-builder tools.

* Build and update landing pages, product pages, blogs, navigation, forms and mobile layouts.

* Manage WordPress themes, plugins, updates, backups and security maintenance.

* Troubleshoot hosting, domains, DNS, SSL certificates and website availability.

* Configure and test supported payment integrations and customer checkout flows. Coordinate account approvals with management and flag anything preventing sales.

* Maintain Google Search Console, submit sitemaps, monitor indexing and resolve technical issues affecting discoverability.

* Maintain redirects, page titles, descriptions and internal links.

* Test booking, inquiry, shopping and checkout journeys after relevant changes.

* Work with our design, content and marketing team to publish accurate, consistent material.

* Keep a task tracker with owners, deadlines, completed links and unresolved blockers.

* Maintain company access and document changes so another team member can support the websites.



Required experience



* Demonstrated Shopify Liquid development experience.

* Strong WordPress development and maintenance skills.

* Working knowledge of hosting, DNS, SSL, backups and technical troubleshooting.

* Experience with Google Search Console and technical SEO.

* Experience testing payment integrations, checkout and website forms.

* Clear written and spoken English.

* Reliable availability, communication and follow-through.



Working expectations



This is a hands-on role supporting existing websites. We are not planning a platform migration as the first assignment.



You must be available during an agreed schedule with overlap with our US team. We use Hubstaff for time tracking and require concise daily progress updates.



If something is blocked, explain the issue, what you have tried and what is needed to resolve it. Problems must be raised before they delay a launch, booking or sale.



To apply, please provide



1. Two live Shopify sites and two WordPress sites you have personally worked on, with a brief explanation of your contribution.

2. One specific example of custom Shopify Liquid work.

3. One example of a payment, hosting or indexing problem you diagnosed and resolved.

4. Your expected monthly compensation for approximately 40 hours per week.

5. Your earliest start date and available working hours, including your time zone.

6. Any other commitments that would affect the proposed schedule.



Please state clearly if your experience is stronger in one platform. We may also consider a dedicated Shopify Liquid specialist alongside a WordPress website manager.

title: Operations Manager/Project Manager
description:
FunnelKween® is a digital growth systems company that helps expert-led brands, entrepreneurs, coaches, consultants, agencies, and growth partners build and operate the backend infrastructure required to execute and scale their revenue-generating campaigns.



Our work extends beyond simply building funnels.



Through **The KWEEN Digital Growth OS™**, we architect, build, connect, operate, and optimize the systems behind webinars, summits, challenges, high-ticket offers, digital products, CRM automation, AI-powered workflows, client portals, and customer experiences.



We operate in a fast-moving environment where multiple client campaigns, technical builds, creative assets, automations, deadlines, and team members must work together.



We are hiring an **Operations & Project Manager** to bring structure, accountability, visibility, and execution discipline across those moving pieces.



---



# THE ROLE



The Operations & Project Manager is responsible for turning strategy into organized execution.



You will serve as the operational bridge between the Founder, internal team members, contractors, and client projects.



When a new campaign, funnel, webinar, automation, client initiative, or internal project is approved, your responsibility is to ensure that:



* The project is properly scoped.

* Deliverables are identified.

* Tasks and subtasks are created.

* Responsibilities are assigned.

* Dependencies are identified.

* Deadlines are established.

* Required assets are collected.

* Team members understand what they are responsible for.

* Progress is monitored.

* Bottlenecks are surfaced early.

* Deliverables are reviewed before being considered complete.

* The Founder has visibility without having to chase the team.

* Clients receive organized communication when appropriate.

* Projects move from strategy to completion.



Your job is not simply to ask, **“Is the task done?”**



Your job is to know:



**What needs to happen next, who owns it, what could block it, when it needs to be completed, and whether the completed work actually meets the project requirements.**



---



# PRIMARY OBJECTIVE



Create an operating environment where the Founder does not have to personally manage every deadline, follow-up, handoff, task, and team member for projects to move forward.



The Founder should be able to establish the strategy and direction while the Operations & Project Manager takes ownership of coordinating execution.



---



# KEY RESPONSIBILITIES



## 1. PROJECT PLANNING & EXECUTION



Take approved initiatives and convert them into clear execution plans.



This includes projects such as:



* Funnel builds

* Webinar campaigns

* Challenges

* Summits

* Masterclasses

* Product launches

* Membership launches

* High-ticket campaigns

* CRM implementations

* Automation projects

* AI workflow implementations

* Client onboarding systems

* Client portals

* Digital product launches

* Internal company initiatives



For every project, you should be able to establish:



* Project objective

* Scope

* Deliverables

* Milestones

* Tasks

* Subtasks

* Dependencies

* Owners

* Priorities

* Due dates

* Approval requirements

* Launch dates

* Testing requirements

* Completion criteria



---



# 2. DAILY TEAM MANAGEMENT



Manage the operational rhythm of the team.



You will:



* Review active projects daily.

* Monitor overdue and upcoming tasks.

* Confirm team priorities.

* Follow up on incomplete work.

* Reassign or escalate tasks when necessary.

* Identify workload conflicts.

* Ensure team members understand their assignments.

* Keep projects moving without waiting for the Founder to intervene.

* Track commitments made during team meetings.

* Hold team members accountable for deadlines.

* Confirm completion rather than assuming completion.



You must be comfortable respectfully asking:



**“What is blocking this?”**



**“What do you need to complete it?”**



**“When will this actually be finished?”**



And then following through.



---



# 3. CAMPAIGN OPERATIONS



Many of our projects involve revenue campaigns.



You will coordinate the operational execution behind:



* Webinars

* Challenges

* Summits

* Workshops

* Masterclasses

* Product launches

* High-ticket enrollment campaigns

* Promotional campaigns



This may involve coordinating:



* Registration pages

* Confirmation pages

* Checkout pages

* Upsells/down-sells

*
 campaigns

* SMS campaigns

* CRM workflows

* Calendars

* Zoom/webinar links

* Communities

* Client portals

* Applications

* Pipelines

* Tracking

* Creative assets

* Videos

* Copy

* Automation

* Integrations

* Testing

* Launch schedules



You do not need to personally build every technical component.



You DO need to understand the project well enough to know what needs to be built, who is responsible for it, how the pieces connect, and whether we are on schedule.



---



# 4. PROJECT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM OWNERSHIP



You will maintain our internal project and task management environment as the operational source of truth.



This includes:



* Creating projects.

* Creating tasks and subtasks.

* Assigning owners.

* Establishing deadlines.

* Updating statuses.

* Documenting requirements.

* Maintaining project notes.

* Tracking dependencies.

* Flagging blocked tasks.

* Tracking approvals.

* Maintaining project timelines.

* Closing completed projects properly.



Our project management system should accurately reflect what is happening in the business at all times.



A team member should not have to attend every meeting to understand the current state of a project.



---



# 5. MEETING-TO-EXECUTION MANAGEMENT



Meetings must result in execution.



You will help ensure that decisions made during:



* Client calls

* Strategy calls

* Team meetings

* Campaign meetings

* Technical meetings

* Founder meetings



are translated into actionable work.



Following meetings, you may be responsible for:



1. Reviewing meeting notes or recordings.

2. Identifying decisions.

3. Extracting action items.

4. Creating tasks.

5. Assigning owners.

6. Establishing deadlines.

7. Updating relevant project documentation.

8. Following through until completion.



Important decisions should not disappear inside meeting recordings or chat messages.



---



# 6. CLIENT PROJECT COORDINATION



You will support the operational side of client relationships.



Depending on the account, this may include:



* Monitoring client deliverables.

* Tracking client approvals.

* Requesting missing assets.

* Coordinating onboarding.

* Maintaining project timelines.

* Preparing project status updates.

* Documenting scope.

* Tracking requests.

* Managing revisions.

* Coordinating internal execution.

* Following up on outstanding client responsibilities.

* Escalating scope or timeline concerns.



You should be able to communicate professionally with clients without creating unnecessary dependency on the Founder.



---



# 7. ASSET & APPROVAL MANAGEMENT



Projects frequently depend on assets from clients, the Founder, designers, copywriters, or technical team members.



You will maintain visibility over:



* Copy

* Photos

* Videos

* Logos

* Brand assets

* Testimonials

* Offer information

* Pricing

* URLs

* Login/access requirements

* Zoom links

* Calendar links

*
/SMS copy

* Creative assets

* Approval requests



You must identify missing assets **before they become launch-day emergencies.**



---



# 8. QUALITY ASSURANCE



“Completed” does not automatically mean “approved.”



Before major deliverables or campaigns are considered ready, you will coordinate QA.



Depending on the project, QA may include checking:



* Links

* Forms

* Buttons

* Mobile responsiveness

* Automations

* Tags

* Pipelines

*
 triggers

* SMS triggers

* Calendars

* Checkout processes

* Payment links

* Redirects

* Confirmation pages

* Webinar access

* Client access

* Community access

* Naming conventions

* Spelling

* Brand consistency

* Required assets

* Tracking



Technical specialists may perform deeper technical testing, but you are responsible for making sure testing actually happens and issues are resolved before launch.



---



# 9. SOP & PROCESS DOCUMENTATION



Help us turn repeatable execution into documented operating procedures.



You will help document processes for recurring activities such as:



* Client onboarding

* Campaign setup

* Webinar launches

* Funnel deployment

* QA

* Client approvals

* Team handoffs

* Asset collection

* Launch preparation

* Post-launch review

* Client offboarding

* Internal task management



When we develop a better way of doing something, that knowledge should become part of the company—not remain inside one person's head.



---



# 10. OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT



Beyond individual client projects, you will help improve how the company itself operates.



This includes:



* Identifying operational bottlenecks.

* Improving workflows.

* Clarifying responsibilities.

* Reducing missed handoffs.

* Eliminating unnecessary manual work.

* Improving documentation.

* Establishing repeatable processes.

* Helping maintain team capacity.

* Improving project visibility.

* Identifying recurring execution problems.

* Recommending operational improvements.



We want someone who does not simply operate within a broken process.



We want someone who notices the broken process and helps improve it.



---



# 11. FOUNDER SUPPORT & EXECUTIVE VISIBILITY



A major purpose of this position is reducing unnecessary operational dependency on the Founder.



You will help the Founder maintain visibility across the company without requiring her to personally chase every project.



You should be able to provide concise updates such as:



### ON TRACK



Projects progressing according to schedule.



### AT RISK



Projects that may miss deadlines without intervention.



### BLOCKED



Projects that cannot progress because of missing assets, decisions, technical issues, or dependencies.



### NEEDS FOUNDER DECISION



Items that genuinely require executive direction.



Do not escalate every small problem.



Solve what you can.



Escalate what requires leadership.



---



# WHAT YOU ARE NOT RESPONSIBLE FOR



This is important.



This position is **not** expected to personally perform every specialized function.



You are not being hired to simultaneously be our:



* Funnel developer

* Graphic designer

* Copywriter

* Automation engineer

* AI developer

* Media buyer

* Video editor



Specialists will execute specialized work.



Your responsibility is ensuring those specialists have what they need and their work connects to the larger project.



---



# WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR



You are likely a strong fit if you are naturally organized but also highly execution-oriented.



You enjoy taking:



**Ideas → Plans → Tasks → Owners → Deadlines → Execution → Completion**



You do not need constant instructions to determine the next logical step.



You anticipate problems.



You follow through.



You communicate clearly.



You pay attention to details.



You can manage multiple projects simultaneously without losing visibility.



You are comfortable working with creative personalities, technical specialists, executives, contractors, and clients.



Most importantly, you understand that project management is not merely updating software.



It is **managing execution.**



---



# REQUIRED SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS



We are looking for someone with experience in several of the following areas:



* Project management

* Operations management

* Digital agency operations

* Online business operations

* Funnel/campaign project management

* Client delivery

* Remote team management

* Launch management

* Process documentation

* Quality assurance

* CRM/funnel environments



You should also demonstrate:



* Excellent written communication

* Excellent verbal communication

* Strong organizational ability

* Strong attention to detail

* Strong follow-through

* Deadline management

* Prioritization

* Problem-solving

* Critical thinking

* Ability to manage multiple simultaneous projects

* Ability to communicate with technical and non-technical team members

* Ability to work independently

* Ability to recognize and escalate risk early



---



# TECHNOLOGY EXPERIENCE



Experience with digital business technology is highly preferred.



Ideal candidates will have familiarity with some combination of:



* GoHighLevel

* ClickUp, Asana, 
, Notion, or similar project management systems

* Slack and/or 

* Google Workspace

* Zoom

* Calendars and scheduling software

* Funnel builders

* CRM systems

*
/SMS automation

* Zapier/Make or similar integration tools

* Skool

* Kajabi

* Stripe

* Webinar platforms

* AI productivity tools

* ChatGPT

* Claude

* Fathom or other AI meeting tools



You do not have to be an engineer.



However, if terms such as **CRM workflow, trigger, automation, funnel, pipeline, webhook, integration, tag, nurture sequence, checkout, API, lead source, client portal, QA, and conversion event** are completely unfamiliar to you, this position is probably not the right fit.



---



# PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES



We are specifically looking for someone who is:



**Proactive**

You identify what needs attention before being asked.



**Accountable**

You take ownership instead of explaining why something was missed.



**Resourceful**

You attempt to solve problems before escalating them.



**Detail-Oriented**

You catch small issues before they become large problems.



**Organized**

You can manage multiple timelines and priorities simultaneously.



**Assertive**

You can respectfully hold people accountable.



**Calm Under Pressure**

Launches and campaigns move quickly. You can prioritize rather than panic.



**Communicative**

You surface problems instead of allowing them to remain hidden.



**Process-Minded**

You naturally look for ways to make execution more repeatable.



**Tech-Comfortable**

You are comfortable learning new systems and working around automation and AI.



**Outcome-Oriented**

You care about whether the project actually gets completed—not merely whether the task was entered into the system.



---



# WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE



Success in this position means:



* Projects have clear owners and deadlines.

* The team knows what it is responsible for.

* Fewer deadlines are missed.

* Fewer tasks fall through the cracks.

* Missing assets are identified earlier.

* Meetings consistently become action items.

* Projects are properly documented.

* Campaigns receive appropriate QA before launch.

* Client requests are tracked.

* Bottlenecks are surfaced quickly.

* The Founder receives clear operational visibility.

* The Founder spends less time chasing execution.

* Team accountability improves.

* SOPs become stronger.

* Campaign execution becomes more predictable.

* Clients receive a more organized experience.



---



# KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS



Performance may be evaluated using metrics such as:



* Percentage of projects delivered on time

* Percentage of milestones completed on time

* Number of overdue tasks

* Average age of overdue tasks

* Number of unidentified/late blockers

* Task completion accuracy

* QA completion rate

* Number of launch-critical errors

* Client asset collection timeliness

* Internal response/follow-up time

* SOP/documentation completion

* Project status accuracy

* Number of issues requiring unnecessary Founder intervention

* Client/project communication consistency



The objective is not simply to produce more activity.



The objective is to create **predictable execution.**



---



# DAILY OPERATING EXPECTATIONS



A typical day may include:



**Beginning of Day**



Review all active projects, deadlines, overdue items, blockers, upcoming launches, and team priorities.



**Throughout the Day**



Coordinate team execution, follow up on tasks, communicate with clients where required, update project records, resolve blockers, manage approvals, coordinate assets, and prepare upcoming work.



**End of Day**



Ensure task statuses accurately reflect reality and identify anything that could affect the next business day.



The Founder should not discover a major deadline problem after it has already become an emergency.



---



# WEEKLY OPERATING EXPECTATIONS



Each week, the Operations & Project Manager should have a clear understanding of:



* What shipped last week

* What did not ship

* Why something was delayed

* What is shipping this week

* Upcoming campaign dates

* Current blockers

* Client dependencies

* Team dependencies

* Projects at risk

* Decisions required from leadership

* Team capacity

* Priority changes



A concise weekly operations report should be maintained for leadership.



---



# 30-DAY EXPECTATIONS



During your first 30 days, you should:



* Learn our company structure.

* Learn our active client accounts.

* Understand our service model.

* Learn our project management environment.

* Understand team roles.

* Review active projects.
